topics.title: Air fryer vs. air-fryer oven: what the capacity figures actually measure
topics.angle: A basket's quarts and an oven's quarts are not the same shape of space. This piece would walk through what each of the three verified capacity figures covers — two 3-qt baskets, a 24.6-litre cavity, one 7.57-litre basket — using the published rows and their manufacturer sources.

topics.title: Two baskets or one big one? The weeknight trade-off, in spec numbers
topics.angle: Compare what the manufacturers state about basket counts, sync features and preset counts, then leave the cooking judgement to the reader — the way the buying guide already does.

topics.title: Preset counts in context: what '4 presets' and '24 presets' actually change
topics.angle: Preset counts are on the spec sheets (4 for the Chefman 8 Qt; 24 and 25 — a published conflict — for the Emeril). A piece explaining what a preset is, and why the Emeril count is printed as a conflict rather than a number, is both useful and honest.

topics.title: How these pages stay honest: reading a spec sheet like an editor
topics.angle: A method piece about this site's own verification rules — every number linked, conflicts published as conflicts, blanks left blank. No product claims at all, so it is the lowest-risk format in the content engine (SG-04 option C).

editorial_note: Fields ending in _editorial are framing, not facts: they restate only what the cited official source already states, and exist to make the pages readable. Where framing and the spec table could ever disagree, the spec table wins — the renderer and the verifier both treat the table as the source of truth.
